newsitem.title: UK: May ex-Soviet oil exports climb to 2.92 mbpd - IEA.
newsitem.headline: May ex-Soviet oil exports climb to 2.92 mbpd - IEA.

text.p: Exports of crude and refined products from the territories of the former Soviet Union rose by 200,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 2.92 million bpd in May, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Friday.
A relatively trouble-free month at Russia's Black Sea port of Novorossiisk more than compensated for lower shipments from the Baltic.

"Exports from the Black Sea increased significantly, by 31 percent to 1.35 million bpd compared with the previous month as there was an absence of the recent obstacles that have constrained exports in recent months: port maintenance, weather delays and work on pipelines serving the port," the IEA said in its Oil Market Report.
Crude oil exports rose by 170,000 bpd to 2.27 million bpd and fuel oil shipments were also higher.
Net product exports at 650,000 bpd were up 20,000 bpd in May.
"Fuel oil exports increased by 51 percent to 400,000 bpd from April levels, offsetting most of the decline of the other products exports," the Paris-based agency said.
Pipeline exports to central and eastern Europe rose by 20,000 bpd to 870,000 bpd.
The IEA said it expected exports to continue to rise over the next three or four months, in line with seasonal trends.
Net exports from the former Soviet Union are expected to rise to three million bpd in 1998 from 2.8 million in 1997, it said.
